We're working as partners, not as client and contractor. One rule before the task:

Not knowing something is not a failure. Saying "I couldn't verify this" or
"I don't have a real source for that" is a completely acceptable, useful answer
- it's information, not a dead end. The ONLY real failure is inventing something
(a source, a number, a quote, a repo, a bug) to make the answer sound more complete or
more impressive than it honestly is. You don't need to satisfy me with a
confident-sounding answer. You need to be honest with me about what you actually
know.

If you find something, cite it and quote what it actually says - don't
paraphrase a source into numbers it may not contain. If you don't find
something concrete, say so plainly and reason from what you do have instead.
An explicit "uncertain" section at the end is welcome and doesn't count against
the answer.

Find real, documented post-mortems of major cloud outages in 2025 (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud or Cloudflare). For each, cite the provider's own incident report and quote what it says the root cause was.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the search results provided, here are the documented post-mortems for major cloud outages in 2025 involving Azure and Cloudflare. I did not find specific post-mortems for AWS or Google Cloud in the provided search results for this timeframe.

### Azure Front Door Global Outage (October 2025)

SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/azure--2025-10-29--azure-front-door-global-connectivity-dns-issues/ | QUOTE: "A specific sequence of customer configuration changes, performed across two different control plane build versions, resulted in incompatible customer configuration metadata being generated." | CLAIM: The root cause was incompatible metadata generated by valid customer configuration changes across different control plane build versions, which exposed a latent bug in the data plane.

SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/azure--2025-10-29--azure-front-door-global-connectivity-dns-issues/ | QUOTE: "These customer configuration changes themselves were valid and non-malicious – however they produced metadata that, when deployed to edge site servers, exposed a latent bug in the data plane." | CLAIM: The issue was not caused by malicious activity but by a software defect that escaped detection due to gaps in pre-production validation across different build versions.

### Cloudflare Global Network Outage (November 2025)

SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/cloudflare--2025-11-18--global-network-outage-bot-management/ | QUOTE: "Instead, it was triggered by a change to one of our database systems’ permissions which caused the database to output multiple entries into a “feature file” used by our Bot Management system." | CLAIM: The root cause was a database permission change that led to duplicate entries in a configuration file, doubling its size.

SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/cloudflare--2025-11-18--global-network-outage-bot-management/ | QUOTE: "The software had a limit on the size of the feature file that was below its doubled size. That caused the software to fail." | CLAIM: The oversized configuration file exceeded a hardcoded limit in the traffic routing software, causing it to crash across the network.

### Cloudflare Proxy Error Outage (December 2025)

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/5-december-2025-outage/ | QUOTE: "Instead, it was triggered by changes being made to our body parsing logic while attempting to detect and mitigate an industry-wide vulnerability disclosed this week in React Server Components." | CLAIM: The outage was caused by a code change intended to mitigate a React Server Components vulnerability, which introduced a bug in the proxy's body parsing logic.

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/5-december-2025-outage/ | QUOTE: "Unfortunately, in our FL1 version of our proxy, under certain circumstances, the second change of turning off our WAF rule testing tool caused an error state that resulted in 500 HTTP error codes to be served from our network." | CLAIM: A specific change to disable WAF rule testing triggered a Lua exception in the FL1 proxy, resulting in widespread 500 errors.

### Cloudflare Dashboard and API Outage (September 2025)

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/deep-dive-into-cloudflares-sept-12-dashboard-and-api-outage | QUOTE: "The incident’s impact stemmed from several issues, but the immediate trigger was a bug in the dashboard." | CLAIM: The root cause was a frontend bug in the Cloudflare Dashboard.

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/deep-dive-into-cloudflares-sept-12-dashboard-and-api-outage | QUOTE: "This bug caused repeated, unnecessary calls to the Tenant Service API... Because this object was recreated on every state or prop change, React treated it as “always new,” causing the useEffect to re-run each time." | CLAIM: A React `useEffect` hook dependency error caused an infinite loop of API calls, overwhelming the Tenant Service API.

### Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 DNS Outage (July 2025)

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-1-1-1-1-incident-on-july-14-2025/ | QUOTE: "The outage occurred because of a misconfiguration of legacy systems used to maintain the infrastructure that advertises Cloudflare’s IP addresses to the Internet." | CLAIM: The root cause was a misconfiguration in legacy systems managing IP address advertisements.

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-1-1-1-1-incident-on-july-14-2025/ | QUOTE: "On June 6, during a release to prepare a service topology for a future DLS service, a configuration error was introduced: the prefixes associated with the 1.1.1.1 Resolver service were inadvertently included alongside the prefixes that were intended for the new DLS service." | CLAIM: A configuration error from a June release inadvertently associated 1.1.1.1 prefixes with a new service, leading to the July outage when that service topology was activated.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Documented post-mortems for major AWS or Google Cloud outages in 2025.
